messages:
anya: Observed a perf regression in continuous-batching replay runs after the kernel-selection change. p95 up ~18% when delay_cap=6ms vs baseline 12ms. Anyone else seeing this?

matt: Did you run apples-to-apples (same model build, same quantization)? which kernel commit?

anya: Yes apples-to-apples. Kernel swap at commit 9f3a2b (select-fusion-refactor). Replay harness = replay_v2 with tenant mix A/B. Config snippet: ```batching:\n  continuous:\n    delay_cap_ms: 6\n    max_batch_tokens: 4096\n    kernel_hint: auto```

raj: What's the kv-cache hit rate? small misses can bloat latency.

anya: KV cache hit dropped from 87% -> 62% for tenant A. Interesting correlation with short delay cap.

ciara: Hmm maybe continuous batching change favors shorter sequences -> more cache thrash? Can you paste perf counters? cpu/gpu timelines?

anya: Attaching short flameview: "gpu_stall_time" spikes on kernel switch, and "memcpy_sync" appears more often. Also saw increased kernel launch count.

lin: Could be kernel selection choosing non-fused attention for short seqs; that has higher launches. Which kernel selected for 512/1024 tokens?

anya: For 512 it picked attn_v2_generic; for 1024 attn_fused. Commit changed heuristic threshold from 768->896.

matt: That explains it. With delay_cap=6ms we pack smaller batches skewed toward 512, so heuristic picks generic.

raj: So two levers: adjust kernel threshold heuristics or tweak batching to avoid small-batch regimes. Which is preferred long-term?

ciara: We should run targeted apples-to-apples: keep kernel selection fixed (force fused) vs let auto. Also run synthetic uniform sequence lengths vs the replay mix.

anya: I ran quick tests: forcing fused for 512 reduces p95 back near baseline, KV cache hit stays at ~84%. Forcing fused done via runtime flag: `--force-kernel=attn_fused`.

matt: Good. Let's also validate on dedicated replay harness with tenant fairness enabled. Need to ensure forcing fused doesn't regress throughput for very short sequences.

lin: Also need to adjust kernel selection logic: don't only use token-length threshold; consider batch-size distribution and kernel launch cost. Something like: if avg_seq*batch_size < threshold, prefer fused.

raj: For KV cache, we should add prefetching for tenants with lots of short-chained requests. Maybe maintain warm cache windows.

anya: Agreed. Action items: 1) run apples-to-apples with force kernel + replay vs synthetic (anya) 2) profile kernel-launch telemetry per tenant (matt) 3) experiment with delay_cap sweep [3,6,12,24] ms and record KV hit + p95 (ciara) 4) propose kernel selection metric change (lin).

matt: I can own telemetry dashboard. Which metrics exactly?

anya: per-tenant: kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_lookups, kernel_choice_histogram, avg_batch_size, p50/p95 latency, kernel_launch_count.

ciara: For the sweep, also capture tail for failure/retry rates.

raj: One more idea: add microburst detector that temporarily raises delay_cap per-tenant when small sequences flood.

lin: Nice. Could be implemented as tenant-weighted delay_cap: delay_cap = base * min(1, alpha * moving_avg_seq)

anya: I'll post initial run results later today.

perf-bot: nightly-replay-run started for thread 1903456789. ETA ~ 3h.

matt: thanks. keep logs small; include config used.

anya: config dump: ```replay:\n  harness=v3\n  tenant_mix=AB\n  seed=42\n  replay_ratio=1.0\n  delay_cap_ms=6\n  max_batch_tokens=4096\n  kernel_policy=auto```

ciara: quick note: avoid changing quantization/compilation flags in apples-to-apples. Keep the exact binary.

lin: Agreed.

matt: tagging infra: @infra if we need extra GPUs for parallel sweeps.

build-bot: build 2026-03-10-9f3a2b passed smoke; artifact uploaded to gs://redwood-artifacts/9f3a2b

anya: thanks all. will update when runs finish."
